description: A button whose caption grows by half again needs somewhere to put it. This one is 129 by 41 and the Spanish runs to fifty-six characters, which will not fit in that box at any size a person can read. There is empty form to its right, so the button takes some of it: a wider button holds the caption on fewer lines, which is what a person actually wants to look at. Widening is capped and rightward only - a button keeps the place it was drawn in, because it is positioned against the thing it acts on. Where there is no room to the right it falls back to growing taller and then to a smaller size, in that order.  A planned_width_at_least of 160 was also asserted here and is removed: the harness never implemented that key, so it had never once been evaluated, and it contradicts the fixture it was written against. This button is drawn with WordWrap on and two lines of height, beside an edit that leaves eighty-nine pixels of gap - so wrapping the caption is honouring what the designer drew, not failing to. What the contract actually guarantees is that the caption fits and the font stays readable, and both of those are checked.
